title: The Snow Queen
text:
A wicked troll once made a mirror that shrank everything good and beautiful and magnified everything ugly. It shattered, and its tiny splinters flew all over the world. Kai, a boy who loved his neighbor and playmate Gerda, got one splinter in his eye and another in his heart. At once he turned cold and mocking. He laughed at Gerda, mimicked old people and found fault with everything.

One winter day the Snow Queen swept him up in her great white sleigh and carried him off to her palace in the far north. Everyone said he was dead. Gerda refused to believe it and set off alone to find him.

Her journey was long. She was held by an old woman with an enchanted garden, helped by a prince and princess, captured by robbers and freed by a wild robber girl, who gave her a reindeer to carry her north. A wise Finnish woman said she could give Gerda no greater power than she already had: her own pure, loving heart.

In the Snow Queen's empty hall of ice Gerda found Kai, blue with cold, trying to arrange pieces of ice into the word Eternity. He did not even know her. Gerda threw her arms around him and wept, and her hot tears ran into his chest and melted the ice in his heart and the splinter with it. Then Kai burst into tears too, and the splinter washed out of his eye. Together they went home, and found that they had grown up, though they were still children at heart.
lesson: When someone you love turns cold, patient and faithful love can sometimes reach them where argument cannot. Do not give up on people too soon.
source: Hans Christian Andersen, The Snow Queen (1844)
